current.issue: Steps 4-7 violate architectural boundary - ML logic in opencode instead of rpc-api

desired.description: OpenCode delegates Thompson Sampling to RPC API
steps: 4. RPC API: Fetch all variants for activity_id from Redis
5. RPC API: For each variant, load metrics (alpha, beta) from Redis
6. RPC API: For each variant, sample_beta(alpha, beta)
7. RPC API: Select variant with highest sample
8. RPC API: Increment selection count in Redis metrics
9. RPC API: Return selected template + selection metadata
10. OpenCode: Receive template from API response
11. OpenCode: Execute activity with selected template
benefits: Clean separation: ML logic stays in rpc-api
OpenCode becomes thinner - just an execution engine
RPC API has full control over selection algorithm
Metrics and sampling logic co-located in same service
Easier to update Thompson Sampling algorithm (one place)
No need to expose raw metrics (alpha, beta) to opencode

architecturalBoundary.principle: ML and probabilistic selection logic belongs in metabob-rpc-api, not metabob-opencode
rationale: Separation of concerns: OpenCode = execution engine, RPC API = intelligence layer
Single source of truth for selection algorithm
Easier to experiment with different selection strategies
Metrics and sampling co-located in same service
enforcement: Code review: Reject PRs adding Beta sampling or Thompson Sampling to opencode
Linting rule: Ban imports of statistical libraries (gamma, beta distributions) in opencode
Architecture tests: Verify no sampling logic in opencode/src/session or opencode/src/ml (except model selection)
